title: Aphorism 1
text: I am for ever walking upon these shores, Betwixt the sand and the foam. The high tide will erase my foot-prints, And the wind will blow away the foam. But the sea and the shore will remain For ever.

title: Aphorism 2
text: Once I filled my hand with mist. Then I opened it, and lo, the mist was a worm. And I closed and opened my hand again, and behold there was a bird. And again I closed and opened my hand, and in its hollow stood a man with a sad face, turned upward. ■ And again I closed my hand, and when 1 opened it there was naught but mist. But I heard a song of exceeding sweetness.

title: Aphorism 3
text: 1 SAND AND FOAM It was but yesterday I thought myself a fragment quivering without rhythm in the sphere of life. • Now I know that I am the sphere, and all life in rhythmic fragments moves within me.

title: Aphorism 4
text: They say to me in their awakening, ‘‘You and the world you live in are but a grain of sand upon the infinite shore of an infinite sea.” And in my dream I say to them, “I am the infinite sea, and all worlds are but grains of sand upon my shore.” + Only once have I been made mute. It was when a man asked me, ‘‘Who are you?”

title: Aphorism 5
text: The first thought of God was an angel. The first word of God was a man. * " We were fluttering, wandering, longing creatures a thousand thousand years before the sea and the wind in the forest gave us words. SAND AND FOAM Now how can we express the ancient of days in us with only the sounds of our yesterdays?

title: Aphorism 6
text: The Sphinx spoke only once, and the Sphinx said, “A grain of sand is a desert, and a desert is a grain of sand; and now let us be silent again.” I heard the Sphinx, but I did not under¬ stand.

title: Aphorism 7
text: Once I saw the face of a woman, and I beheld all her children not yet born. And a woman looked upon my face and she knew all my forefathers, dead before she was born.

title: Aphorism 8
text: Now would I fulfil myself. But how shall I unless I become a planet with intelligent lives dwelling upon it? Is not this every man’s goal? ■ ★ ■ ' A pearl is a temple built by pain around a grain of sand. 3 SAND AND FOAM What longing built our bodies and around what grains?

title: Aphorism 9
text: When God threw me, a pebble, into this wondrous lake I disturbed its surface with countless circles. , t T , But when I reached the depths I became very still.

title: Aphorism 10
text: Give me silence and I will outdare the night.

title: Aphorism 11
text: I had a second birth when my soul and my body loved one another and were married.

title: Aphorism 12
text: Once I knew a man whose ears were exceed¬ ingly keen, but he was dumb. He had lost his tongue in a battle. I know now what battles that man fought before the great silence came. I am glad he is dead The world is not large enough for two ol us.

title: Aphorism 13
text: 4 SAND AND FOAM Long did I lie in the dust of Egypt, silent and unaware of the seasons. . .Then the sun gave me birth, and I rose and walked upon the banks of the Nile, Singing with the days and dreaming with the nights. And now the sun treads upon me with a thousand feet that I may lie again in the dust of Egypt. But behold a marvel and a riddle! The very sun that gathered me cannot scatter me. Still erect am I, and sure of foot do I walk upon the banks of the Nile.

title: Aphorism 14
text: Remembrance is a form of meeting.

title: Aphorism 15
text: Forgetfulness is a form of freedom. + We measure time according to the move¬ ment of countless suns; and they measure time by little machines in their little pockets. Now tell me, how could we ever meet at the same place and the same time?

title: Aphorism 16
text: 5 SAND AND FOAM Space is not space between the earth and the sun to one who looks down from the windows of the Milky Way. • -

title: Aphorism 17
text: Humanity is a river of light running from ex-eternity to eternity.

title: Aphorism 18
text: Do not the spirits who dwell in the ether envy man his pain?

title: Aphorism 19
text: On my way to the Holy City 1 met another pilgrim and I asked him, "Is this indeed the way to the Holy City?” And he said, “Follow me, and you will reach the Holy City in a day and a night. And I followed him. And we walked many days and many nights, yet we did not reach the Holy City. And what was to my surprise, he became angry with me because he had misled me.

title: Aphorism 20
text: ' Make me, O God, the prey of the lion, ere You make the rabbit my prey.

title: Aphorism 21
text: 6 My house says to me, “Do not leave me, for here dwells your past.” And the road says to me, “Come and follow me, for I am your future.” And I say to both my house and the road, “I have no past, nor have I a future. If I stay here, there is a going in my staying; and if I go there is a staying in my going. Only love and death change all things.”

title: Aphorism 22
text: How can I lose faith in the justice of life, when the dreams of those who sleep upon feathers are not more beautiful than the dreams of those who sleep upon the earth?

title: Aphorism 23
text: Strange, the desire for certain pleasures is a part of my pain.

title: Aphorism 24
text: Seven times have I despised my soul: 7 SAND AND FOAM The first time when I saw her being meek that she might attain height. The second time when I saw her limping- before the crippled. The third time when she was given to choose between the hard and the easy, and she chose the easy. The fourth time when she committed a wrong, and comforted herself that others also commit wrong. The fifth time when she forbore for weakness, and attributed her patience to strength. The sixth time when she despised the ugli¬ ness of a face, and knew not that it was one of her own masks. And the seventh time when she sang a song of praise, and deemed it a virtue.

title: Aphorism 25
text: I am ignorant of absolute truth. But I am humble before my ignorance, and therein lies my honour and my reward.

title: Aphorism 26
text: There is a space between man’s imagination 8 i'arauise is there, behind that door, In the next room; but I have lost the key. Perhaps I have only mislaid it.

title: Aphorism 27
text: You are blind and I am deaf and dumb, so let us touch hands and understand.

title: Aphorism 28
text: The significance of man is not in what he attains, but rather in what he longs to attain.

title: Aphorism 29
text: Some of us are like ink and some like paper. And if it were not for the blackness of some of us, some of us would be dumb. And if it were not for the whiteness of some of us, some of us would be blind. + Give me an ear and I will give you a voice. + Our mind is a sponge; our heart is a stream. 9 SAND AND FOAM Is it not strange that most of us choose suck¬ ing rather than running?

title: Aphorism 30
text: When you long for blessings that you may not name, and when you grieve knowing not the cause, then indeed you are growing with all things that grow, and rising toward your greater self.

title: Aphorism 31
text: When one is drunk with a vision, lie deems his faint expression of it the very wine.

title: Aphorism 32
text: You drink wine that you may be in¬ toxicated; and I drink that it may sober me from that other wine.

title: Aphorism 33
text: When my cup is empty I resign myself to its emptiness; but when it is half full I resent its half-fullness.

title: Aphorism 34
text: The reality of the' other person is not in what he reveals to you, but in what he cannot reveal to you. 10 facing page ^ SAND AND FOAM j SAND AND FOAM Therefore, if you would understand him, listen not to w 1 at he says but rather to what he does not say.

title: Aphorism 35
text: Half of whit I say is meaningless; but I say it so that the other half may reach you.

title: Aphorism 36
text: A sense of humour is a sense of proportion.

title: Aphorism 37
text: My loneliness was born when men praised my talkative faults and blamed my silent virtues.

title: Aphorism 38
text: When Life does not find a singer to sing her heart she produces a philosopher to speak her mind. A truth is to be known always, to be uttered ..sometimes. ■*'' * r The real in us is silent; the acquired is talkative.

title: Aphorism 39
text: 11 * SAND AND FOAM The voice of life in me cannot reach the ear of life in you; but let us talk that we may not feel lonely.

title: Aphorism 40
text: When two women talk they say nothing; when one woman speaks she reveals all of lif e.

title: Aphorism 41
text: Frogs may bellow louder than bulls, but they cannot drag the plough in the field nor turn the wheel of the winepress, and ot their skins you cannot make shoes.

title: Aphorism 42
text: Only the dumb envy the talkative.

title: Aphorism 43
text: If winter should say, “Spring is in my heart,” who would believe winter?

title: Aphorism 45
text: Should you really open your eyes and see, you would behold your image in all images. 12 SAND AND FOAM And should you open your ears and listen, you would hear your own voice in all voices.

title: Aphorism 46
text: It takes two of us to discover truth: one to utter it and one to understand it.

title: Aphorism 47
text: Though the wave of words is for ever upon us, yet our depth is for ever silent.

title: Aphorism 48
text: Many a doctrine is like a window pane. We see truth through it, but it divides us from truth.

title: Aphorism 49
text: s # • Now let us play hide and seek. .Should you hide in my heart it wouITnotfbe difficult to find you. But should you hide behind your own shell, then It would be useless for anyone to seek you.

title: Aphorism 50
text: A woman may veil her face with a smile.

title: Aphorism 51
text: 13 SAND AND FOAM How noble is the sad heart who would smg a joyous song with joyous hearts.

title: Aphorism 52
text: He who would understand a woman, or dissect senius, or solve the mystery of silence fs the very man who would wake from a beautiful dream to sit at a breakfast table.

title: Aphorism 53
text: I would walk with all those who walk. I would not stand still to watch the procession passing by.

title: Aphorism 54
text: You owe more than gold to him who serves you. Give him of your heart or serve him.

title: Aphorism 55
text: Nay, we have not lived in vain. Have they not built towers of our bones? Let us not be particular and sectional. TTi pet’s mind and the scorpion’s tail rise in glory rom the same earth. 14 SAND AND FOAM Every dragon gives birth to a St. George who slays it.

title: Aphorism 56
text: Trees are poems that the earth writes upon the sky. We fell them down and turn them into paper that we may record our emptiness.

title: Aphorism 57
text: Should you care to w T rite (and only the saints know why you should) you must needs have knowledge and art and magic—the knowledge of the music of words, the art of being artless, and the magic of loving your readers. writing a poem and the ecstasy of a poem un m SAND AND FOAM But you and all my neighbours agree that 1 always choose badly*

title: Aphorism 58
text: Poetry Is not an opinion expressed. It Is a son rS rises from a bleeding wound or a smiling mouth.

title: Aphorism 59
text: Words are timeless. You should utter them or write them with a knowledge of their time¬ lessness.

title: Aphorism 60
text: A poet is a dethroned king sitting among the ashes of his palace trying to fashion an image nut of the ashes. Poetry is a deal of joy and pain and wonder, with a dash of the dictionary. 4 In vain shall a poet seek the mother of the songs of his heart. 16 SAND AND FOAM Once I said to a poet, “We shall not know your worth until you die.” And he answered, saying, “Yes, death is always the revealer. And if indeed you would know my worth, it is that I have more in my heart than upon my tongue, and more in my desire than in my hand.”

title: Aphorism 61
text: If you sing of beauty, though alone in the heart of the desert, you will have an audience.

title: Aphorism 62
text: Poetry is wisdom that enchants the heart Wisdom is poetry that sings in the mind. If we could enchant man’s heart and at the same time sing in his mind, Then in truth he would live in the shadow of God.

title: Aphorism 63
text: Inspiration will always sing; inspiration will never explain.

title: Aphorism 64
text: We often sing lullabies to our children that we ourselves may sleep.

title: Aphorism 65
text: 17 SAND AND FOAM All our words are but crumbs that f all down from the feast of the mind.

title: Aphorism 66
text: Thinking is always the stumbling stone to poetry.

title: Aphorism 67
text: A great singer is he who sings our silences.

title: Aphorism 68
text: How can you sing if your mouth be filled W1 How°shall your hand be raised in blessing if it is filled with gold?

title: Aphorism 69
text: They say the nightingale pierces his bosom with a thorn when he sings a love song. So do we all. How else should we sing?

title: Aphorism 70
text: Genius is but a robin’s song at the beginning of a slow spring. Even the most winged spirit cannot escape physical necessity. + 18 SAND AND FOAM A madman is not less a musician than you or myself; only the instrument on which he plays is a little out of tune.

title: Aphorism 71
text: The song that lies silent in the heart of a mother smgs upon the lips of her child.

title: Aphorism 72
text: No longing remains unfulfilled. -

title: Aphorism 73
text: I have never agreed with my other self wholly. The truth of the matter seems to lie between us.

title: Aphorism 74
text: Your other self is always sorry for you. But your other self grows on sorrow; so all is well. There is no struggle of soul and body save in the minds of those whose souls are asleep and whose bodies are out of tune.

title: Aphorism 75
text: When you reach the heart of life you shall 19 SAND AND FOAM find beauty in all things, even in the eyes that are blind to beauty.

title: Aphorism 76
text: We live only to discover beauty. All else is a form of waiting.

title: Aphorism 77
text: Sow a seed and the earth will yield you a flower. Dream your dream to the sky and it will bring you your beloved.

title: Aphorism 78
text: The devil died the very day you were horn. Now you do not have to go through hell to meet an angel.

title: Aphorism 79
text: Many a woman borrows a man s heart; very few could possess it.

title: Aphorism 80
text: If you would possess you must not claim. When a man’s hand touches the hand or a woman they both touch the heart of eternity.

title: Aphorism 81
text: 20 b AND AND FOAM Love is the veil between lover and lover.

title: Aphorism 82
text: Every man loves two women; the one is the creation of his imagination, and the other is not yet born.

title: Aphorism 83
text: Men who do not forgive women their little faults will never enjoy their great virtues.

title: Aphorism 84
text: Love that does not renew itself every day becomes a habit and in turn a slavery.

title: Aphorism 85
text: Lovers embrace that which is between them rather than each other.

title: Aphorism 86
text: Love and doubt have never been on speak¬ ing terms.

title: Aphorism 87
text: Love is a word of light, written by a hand of light, upon a page of light. ★ . . 21 SAND AND FOAM Friendship is always a sweet responsibility, never an opportunity.

title: Aphorism 88
text: If you do not understand your friend under all conditions you will never understand him.

title: Aphorism 89
text: Your most radiant garment is of the other PC Yom mo^voury meal is that which you eat at the other person’s table; _ . , Your most comfortable bed is m the other Pe Now tSfrne, how can you separate your¬ self from the other person?

title: Aphorism 90
text: Your mind and my heart will never agree until your mind ceases to live m numbers and my heart in the mist. . ★ ' We shall never understand one another until we reduce the language to seven words. 22 SAND AND FOAM How shall my heart be unsealed unless it be broken?

title: Aphorism 91
text: Only great sorrow or great joy can reveal your truth. If you would be revealed you must either dance naked in the sun, or carry your cross.

title: Aphorism 92
text: Should Nature heed what we say of con¬ tentment no river would seek the sea, and no winter would turn to spring. Should she heed all we say of thrift, how many of us would be breathing this air?

title: Aphorism 93
text: You see but your shadow when you turn your back to the sun.

title: Aphorism 94
text: You are free before the sun of the day, and free before the stars of the night; And you are free when there is no sun and no moon and no star. You are even free when you close your eyes upon all there is. 23 SAND AND FOAM But you are a slave to him whom you love be Md rskve T to h hhn who loves you because he loves you.

title: Aphorism 95
text: We are all beggars at the gate oli the _trnipk, and each one of us receives his share ot the bounty of the King when he enters the temple, *1" lu ieabus of one another, which is another way of belittling the King.

title: Aphorism 96
text: You cannot consume beyond your appetite. The oth« half of the loaf belongs to the other person, and there should remarn a little bread for the chance guest.

title: Aphorism 97
text: If it were not for guests, all houses would be graves.

And he answered him and said: “Did I not speak of freedom, and of the mist which is our greater freedom? Yet it is in pain I make pilgrim¬ age to the isle where I was born, even like unto a ghost of one slain come to kneel before those who have slain him.”

Then a cry came from the people, and it was a cry of remembrance and of entreaty.

And he looked upon his mariners and said: “And what have I brought them? A hunter was I, in a distant land. With aim and might I have spent the golden arrows they gave me, but I have brought down no game. I followed not the arrows. Mayhap they are spreading now in the sun with the pinions of wounded eagles that would not fall to earth. And mayhap the arrow¬ heads have fallen into the hands of those who had need of them for bread and wine.

“Even so, love’s hand is still upon me, and you, my mariners, still sail my vision, and I shall not be dumb. I shall cry out when the hand of the seasons is upon my throat, and I shall sing my words when my lips are burned with flames/*

And they were troubled in their hearts because he spoke these things. And one said: “Master, teach us all, and mayhap because your blood flows in our veins, and our breath is of your fragrance, we shall understand.’*

Then he answered them, and the wind was in his voice, and he said: “Brought you me to the isle of my birth to be a teacher? Not yet have I been caged by wisdom. Too young am I and too verdant to speak of aught but self, which is for ever the deep calling upon the deep.

“Let him who would have wisdom seek it in the buttercup or in a pinch of red clay. I am still the singer. Still I shall sing the earth, and I shall sing your lost dreaming that walks the day between sleep and sleep. But I shall gaze upon the sea.”

“Go you upon your way with singing, but let each song be brief, for only the songs that die young upon your lips shall live in human hearts.

“Tell a lovely truth in little words, but never an ugly truth in any words. Tell the maiden whose hair shines in the sun that she is the daughter of the morning. But if you shall behold the sightless, say not to him that he is one with night.

“Listen to the flute-player as it were listening to April, but if you shall hear the critic and the fault-finder speak, be deaf as your own bones and as distant as your fancy.

“I go> but if I go with a truth not yet voiced, that very truth will again seek me and gather me, though my elements be scattered throughout the silences of eternity, and again shall I come before you that I may speak with a voice born anew out of the heart of those boundless silences.

“And if there be aught of beauty that I have declared not unto you, then once again shall I be called, ay, even by mine own name, Almustafa, and I shall give you a sign, that you may know I have come back to speak all that is lacking, for God will not suffer Himself to be hidden from man, nor His word to lie covered in the abyss of the heart of man.

And he who sang his song to the wind shall sing it also to the moving spheres.”
